recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up core source work is needed for FHIR-5195 unless PA explicitly reopens the date-only birthDate policy for practitioner/person resources.
issue_request: FHIR-5195 was a Published PA change request from the Jan 2015 ballot. It asked whether Practitioner.birthDate should match Patient.birthDate by changing from dateTime to date, and comments also asked for Person consistency. The final Persuasive with Modification resolution changed Practitioner.birthDate from datetime to Date to avoid timezone shifts and accidental duplicate records when birth dates are used for identification.
initial_application: The issue appears to have been applied by git commit 8ed9982708ac31ba37ad6670f9be8ba628634329, whose message explicitly lists tracker 5195 among Practitioner ballot reconciliation issues. Its patch changed the Practitioner spreadsheet birthDate type cell from dateTime to date. Person alignment was handled by the later same-family FHIR-7311 commit 0522d003c90c49a5774028204610056c3360d1c6, which is already audited on the combined branch.
additional_context: Practitioner, Person, Patient, and RelatedPerson are active current-build resources in source/fhir.ini. The current StructureDefinition sources type Practitioner.birthDate, Person.birthDate, Patient.birthDate, and RelatedPerson.birthDate as date. FHIR-7311 is the directly related Published issue for Person consistency and already has commit 78f16b075fd9d7b8a85f7cc9fa7051e3ca29aaff on the combined branch. Zulip and Confluence searches found no directly relevant FHIR-5195 discussion or minutes that would change the Jira/source/history conclusion.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the authoritative current source already implements the FHIR-5195 decision. No source edit is needed.

related_jiras.note: Later Published PA issue resolved the Person side of the same birthDate consistency question by changing Person.birthDate to date; it is already represented on the combined branch.
Reinstated Person with an initial dateTime birthDate, explaining why later FHIR-5195/FHIR-7311 alignment was needed, but it is broader than this reconciliation.
